title: The old system gets the final word
summary: A lifetime simulation finds that financial-advice prompts can compound into unequal outcomes, Frontis trains a machine-learning improver around the same operations its search harness uses, and the Locksmith Loop makes generated Java answer to the COBOL behavior it replaces. Plus two smaller research signals on repository context and compact robot policies.

dives.story: AI financial advice as a lifetime simulation, and the prompt gap that compounds
dives.why_it_matters: Teams building high-stakes assistants need to know whether ordinary users receive systematically worse advice because the interface expects expert-level prompts or the model silently changes recommendations based on demographic cues.

dives.story: Frontis-MA1 and OpenMLE train the same program-evolution operators used during long-horizon search
dives.why_it_matters: Machine-learning and agent-platform teams care because aligning post-training with the harness's actual Draft, Improve, Debug, and Crossover moves increased measured task performance while structured experience improved useful discoveries per token.

dives.story: The Locksmith Loop uses deterministic parity to validate agentic COBOL-to-Java migration
dives.why_it_matters: Organizations modernizing legacy systems need generated replacements to reproduce obscure operational behavior before cutover, and this pattern lets agents expand the test space without letting a model decide whether its own output is correct.

concepts_taught: demand-versus-supply decomposition for prompt-conditioned AI advice: separating differences in what user groups ask from differences in what a model recommends for the same prompt under randomized demographic labels
meta-evolution in executable machine-learning engineering: post-training the same Draft, Improve, Debug, and Crossover transformations that an inference-time search harness composes
differential parity testing with symmetric harness mutation: using a legacy executable as a compatibility oracle while an agent opens otherwise unreachable test paths on both reference and target
